primitives.name: Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Denoising Encoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Stage 1 — ASTGCN denoising encoder: 3 Adaptive ST-GCN blocks with Chebyshev filters of order 7 and 64-d features, followed by an MLP projecting to a 40-d latent space.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'temporal frames', 'J': 'joints in skeleton', 'd_{\\text{lat}}': 'latent dimension (40)', '\\mathcal{X}': 'input 2D joint coordinates', '\\mathcal{Z}': 'denoised latent pose embedding'}
primitives.assumptions: Pose data is temporally ordered, joints are connected in a fixed topology, and noise injection enables robust latent learning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pose estimation quality degrades below threshold, denoising fails and latent space becomes misaligned.

layer2.mapping: Maps raw 2D skeletal sequences to a compact, noise-resilient latent space suitable for downstream phase clustering.

primitives.name: Structured Unbalanced Optimal Transport for Phase Assignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: Stage 2 — Structured unbalanced OT: visual cost is cosine distance between latent embeddings; the OT objective combines (i) a fused Gromov-Wasserstein temporal-structure term, (ii) a Kantorovich appearance-cost term, and (iii) a KL relaxation toward a prior class distribution.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{T}': 'transport plan matrix', '\\mathbf{C}_t': 'temporal structure cost matrix', '\\mathbf{C}_a': 'appearance cost matrix', '\\mathbf{P}': 'prior class distribution', '\\alpha, \\beta': 'weighting parameters'}
primitives.assumptions: Phases are temporally ordered, appearance and structure costs are separable, and a prior over class proportions exists.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When phase boundaries are ambiguous or class priors are inaccurate, transport plan degenerates into uniform assignment.

layer2.mapping: Maps latent pose embeddings to discrete biomechanical phases via optimal transport, preserving temporal continuity and appearance consistency.
layer2.telemetry: mIoU, F1 score, boundary alignment accuracy.

primitives.name: Pseudo-Label Cross Entropy Closure Loop
primitives.verbatim_quote: A pseudo-label cross-entropy loss (labels from the transport plan) closes the unsupervised loop.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_{\\theta}(y_t | z_t)': 'predicted phase probability given latent vector', 'y_t': 'pseudo-labeled phase at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Transport plan provides reliable pseudo-labels, model is expressive enough to learn from them.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If transport plan is inaccurate, pseudo-labels introduce error propagation and degrade model performance.

layer2.telemetry: Cross-entropy loss convergence, phase purity over iterations.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology employs a two-stage pipeline: first, an ASTGCN encoder denoises and embeds 2D skeletal sequences into a 40-dimensional latent space. This stage uses Chebyshev filters and temporal windows to capture spatial and temporal dependencies. Second, structured unbalanced optimal transport (OT) assigns frames to biomechanical phases by minimizing a composite cost function combining temporal structure (Gromov-Wasserstein), appearance (Kantorovich), and prior class distributions (KL divergence). The transport plan is refined via pseudo-label cross-entropy, closing the unsupervised loop. The method assumes K known phases, temporal ordering, and sufficient pose quality. Failures occur when pose estimation is poor, phase boundaries are ill-defined, or priors mismatch reality. The approach is mathematically grounded in graph signal processing and optimal transport theory, offering a principled way to segment motion without supervision.
